sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantan.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: You may have noticed that our modern world is saturated with awards.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经注意到，我们现代世界充斥着各种奖项。

sentences.en: Welcome to the 77th Annual Peabody Awards.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到第77届年度皮博迪奖。

sentences.en: Welcome to the 2019 Golden Glove Awards.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到2019年金球奖。

sentences.en: The Miss Universe Crafts.
sentences.zh: 环球小姐手工艺奖。

sentences.en: The 5th Annual Tony Awards.
sentences.zh: 第五届年度托尼奖。

sentences.en: Teacher of the Annual Igno Bell Prize.
sentences.zh: 搞笑诺贝尔奖年度教师。

sentences.en: Life Achievement Award.
sentences.zh: 终身成就奖。

sentences.en: Live from Copenhagen!
sentences.zh: 哥本哈根现场直播！

sentences.en: Many of these awards have been created in the past century.
sentences.zh: 其中许多奖项都是在过去一个世纪里创立的。

sentences.en: But awards have been around for millennia.
sentences.zh: 但奖项的存在已有数千年历史。

sentences.en: The Greeks and Romans had them.
sentences.zh: 希腊人和罗马人就拥有它们。

sentences.en: Kings and queens have long given them to their bravest warriors.
sentences.zh: 国王和王后长期以来一直将它们授予最勇敢的战士。

sentences.en: Societies all over the world have recognized their best citizens with prizes.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的社会都用奖品来表彰他们最优秀的公民。

sentences.en: We pay tribute to those distinguished individuals with our nation's highest civilian honor,
sentences.zh: 我们以国家最高平民荣誉向这些杰出个人致敬，

sentences.en: the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
sentences.zh: 即总统自由勋章。

sentences.en: Awards are so ubiquitous that we rarely stop to ask, do they work?
sentences.zh: 奖项如此无处不在，以至于我们很少停下来思考：它们真的有用吗？

sentences.en: Do prizes inspire and motivate?
sentences.zh: 奖品能带来启发和动力吗？

sentences.en: Or do they cause jealousy and resentment?
sentences.zh: 还是会引发嫉妒和怨恨？

sentences.en: The Upside, the Downside, and the Psychology of Awards.
sentences.zh: 奖项的积极面、消极面及其背后的心理学。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Bruno Frey is an economist who has spent years studying how prizes shape human behavior.
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺·弗雷是一位经济学家，多年来一直研究奖项如何塑造人类行为。

sentences.en: He works at the University of Basel in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 他在瑞士巴塞尔大学工作。

sentences.en: Along with Yana Gallus, he is co-author of the book, Honours vs. Money, The Economics of Awards.
sentences.zh: 他和亚娜·加吕斯合著了《荣誉与金钱：奖项经济学》一书。

sentences.en: Getting an award makes people feel good.
sentences.zh: 获奖让人感觉良好。

sentences.en: But Bruno says the real benefits of awards are seen long after that initial glow wears off.
sentences.zh: 但布鲁诺表示，奖项的真正好处是在最初的喜悦消散很久之后才显现出来的。

sentences.en: When people are given an award in general, they are likely to work better, to be more engaged,
sentences.zh: 当人们普遍获得奖项时，他们往往工作得更好、参与度更高、

sentences.en: to have, as we say, higher intrinsic motivation.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，拥有更高的内在动力。

sentences.en: That is, they like to work and they like to do what they do and therefore are contributing really to the social good.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们喜欢工作，喜欢做自己正在做的事，因此真正为社会公益做出了贡献。

sentences.en: An important reason awards have this effect is that they are deeply social.
sentences.zh: 奖项产生这种效果的一个重要原因在于它们具有深刻的社会属性。

sentences.en: Awards are handed out in settings where you are surrounded by your peers.
sentences.zh: 奖项是在你被同龄人环绕的环境中颁发的。

sentences.en: An award can make you feel appreciated by people whose opinions you value.
sentences.zh: 奖项能让你感受到那些你所珍视其观点的人对你的认可。

sentences.en: In this regard, an award is very different than a cash bonus.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，奖项与现金奖金有着本质的区别。

sentences.en: Normally, people are not allowed to say how large the bonuses they receive.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，人们不允许透露他们获得的奖金有多大。

sentences.en: So, it is unknown to other people.
sentences.zh: 因此，其他人对此并不知情。

sentences.en: While awards are always given in a ceremony, sometimes in a lavish one, sometimes in a smaller one,
sentences.zh: 虽然奖项总是在仪式上颁发，有时极其奢华，有时较为小型，

sentences.en: but it's always with other people around.
sentences.zh: 但总是有其他人陪伴在周围。

sentences.en: And the person or the organization giving the award specifies exactly why the person or the organization gets the award.
sentences.zh: 颁发奖项的个人或组织会明确说明获得该奖项的人或组织为何获奖。

sentences.en: And this emphasizes the extraordinary engagement of the people receiving the awards.
sentences.zh: 这突显了获奖者非凡的投入。

sentences.en: And that tends to raise the intrinsic motivation because it's recognized, because it's appreciated.
sentences.zh: 这往往会提高内在动力，因为这种付出得到了认可和感激。

sentences.en: One of the things that you and others have learned is that people care intensely about the prestige that awards can confer.
sentences.zh: 你和其他人了解到的情况之一是，人们对奖项所能赋予的声望极其看重。

sentences.en: Perhaps even more than money, prizes provide glory.
sentences.zh: 奖品带来的荣耀甚至可能超过金钱。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the world of golf.
sentences.zh: 我想播放一段高尔夫球坛的音频剪辑。

sentences.en: This is the 2017 PGA Championship winner, Justin Thomas.
sentences.zh: 这是2017年PGA锦标赛冠军贾斯汀·托马斯。

sentences.en: In terms of this week, it's definitely not about the money.
sentences.zh: 就本周而言，这绝对不是为了钱。

sentences.en: It's definitely not about being better than anybody else.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是为了比任何人表现得更好。

sentences.en: Like I said earlier, I just like to win, and I like trophies.
sentences.zh: 就像我刚才说的，我就是喜欢赢，我喜欢奖杯。

sentences.en: So, I just want to win just to go win not only the Tour Championship,
sentences.zh: 所以，我只想赢，不仅是为了赢得巡回锦标赛，

sentences.en: but anytime you can win a year-long race and be known as a champion of an entire year, it's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 而且无论何时，只要你能赢得全年的赛事并被称为整整一年的冠军，这就是一件大事。

sentences.en: So, that to me is what I would be most excited about.
sentences.zh: 所以，对我来说，这才是让我最兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: Bruno, do you see other examples of people who actually prefer prestige and glory to money?
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺，你还见过哪些人更喜欢声望和荣耀而非金钱的例子吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are very many instances of that.
sentences.zh: 这样的例子非常多。

sentences.en: Just consider if you want to invite a famous person, let's say, coming from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，如果你想邀请一位名人，比方说从美国邀请到欧洲，或者从欧洲邀请到美国。

sentences.en: to Europe or from Europe to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果这个人已经有了很高的收入、很好的收入，那么你很难请动他们。

sentences.en: If that person has a high income already, a good income, then it's very difficult to get people.
sentences.zh: 有一个很好的例子，那就是罗杰·费德勒，瑞士名人之一。

sentences.en: There is a nice example, namely Roger Federer, one of the famous Swiss.
sentences.zh: 他大约赚了9300万美元，我认为你无法用任何东西引诱他去任何地方。

sentences.en: He earns about $93 million, and I don't think that you can induce him to go anywhere to get anything.
sentences.zh: 但当你给他一个不错的奖项时，你就有更大的机会做到这一点。

sentences.en: But when you offer him a nice award, you have a better chance to do that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你在书里讨论的另一个领域，也就是说，获奖不仅对个人有益，

sentences.en: I'm wondering about another area that you discuss in the book, which is it's not just a benefit to individuals who win awards,
sentences.zh: 对组织也有好处，特别是如果你是一个资金并不充裕的组织，

sentences.en: but there are benefits to organizations as well, especially if you're an organization that doesn't necessarily have a lot of money
sentences.zh: 或者你没有足够的余地付给人们很多钱。

sentences.en: or you don't have the leeway to pay people a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 奖项确实是提高动力的强有力方式。

sentences.en: Awards are really a powerful way to increase motivation.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，它还在颁奖者和接受者之间建立了一种忠诚的纽带。

sentences.en: Yes, indeed, and it also creates a bond of loyalty between the giver and the recipient.
sentences.zh: 你不能接受英国女王授予的勋章，然后又说她是个愚蠢的女人，或者我不在乎奖项，

sentences.en: You cannot accept the order by the Queen of England and then say she's a silly woman or I don't care about awards
sentences.zh: 因为那样人们会问：那你当初为什么要接受？

sentences.en: because then people say, why did you accept it?
sentences.zh: 但人们确实会接受奖项。

sentences.en: But people do accept awards.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有不接受奖项的情况，但总的来说，人们会接受奖项。

sentences.en: Of course, there are cases in which awards are not accepted, but in general, people accept the awards.
sentences.zh: 随后便会产生一种新的忠诚纽带，与颁奖者建立起特殊的联系。

sentences.en: And then there is a new bond of loyalty, a special relationship to the one who gives the award.
sentences.zh: 这在以营利为目的的资本主义企业中同样重要。

sentences.en: And that is also important in for-profit capitalist enterprises.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否正是军队中为什么有如此众多奖项的原因之一，

sentences.en: I'm wondering if this might be one of the reasons why you have so many awards in military service especially,
sentences.zh: 因为这不仅是对做出重要贡献的人给予表彰，

sentences.en: because it's not just that you're conferring recognition on people who have done important things,
sentences.zh: 而且还能建立这种关系纽带，即上级和下属之间的联系，

sentences.en: but building those bonds of relationships, the connections between superiors and subordinates,
sentences.zh: 这对于一支成功的军队来说实际上至关重要。

sentences.en: that is actually essential for a successful military.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，特别是在军事领域，很难界定一个好士兵、

sentences.en: Indeed, and especially in the military sector, it's difficult to define what a good soldier,
sentences.zh: 一个好军官、一个好将军必须做什么，因为这些无法提前规定。

sentences.en: a good officer, a good general must do because you cannot fix that in advance.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须信任这些人，相信他们会做正确的事情。

sentences.en: So you must rely on the persons to do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 你怎么能为勇敢、忠诚或正直标上价格呢？

sentences.en: And how do you put a price on bravery or loyalty or integrity?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是不可能的，因为勇敢究竟值1000万美元、5000美元还是多少？

sentences.en: Yes, that's not possible because is bravery $10 million or $5,000 or whatever?
sentences.zh: 没人知道。

sentences.en: One doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你授予一枚勋章，然后在仪式上说：

sentences.en: While if you give an order and then in the ceremony you say,
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，这位士兵做出了超出职责范围的事情，做出了非凡的举动，这足以让获奖者感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: oh yes, the soldiers did something beyond his duty, something extraordinary that is totally sufficient to make the recipient very happy.
sentences.zh: 你们在维基百科网站上对奖项进行了一项实地实验。

sentences.en: You conducted a field experiment on awards with the site Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 这是德语版的维基百科。

sentences.en: This was the German language Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 在维基百科上，这是一个在线百科全书，每个条目都由编辑和读者众包完成。

sentences.en: And in Wikipedia, of course, it's the online encyclopedia where each article is crowdsourced by editors and readers.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个实地实验以及你们发现了什么。

sentences.en: Tell me about the field experiment and what you found.
sentences.zh: 我们引入了一项新奖项。

sentences.en: We introduced a new award.
sentences.zh: 实际上是我们自己发明了一个，我们将这个奖项颁发给那些持续为维基百科贡献作品的人，

sentences.en: We invented one, actually, and we gave this award to people who continued contributing work to Wikipedia
sentences.zh: 因为我们观察到（这也是维基百科的一个问题），很多人贡献了一篇文章然后就停手了。

sentences.en: because we observed, or that is a problem of Wikipedia, that a lot of people contribute one article and then stop.
sentences.zh: 于是我们引入了一个名为“雪绒花”的奖项。

sentences.en: So we introduced an award which is called Edelweiss.
sentences.zh: 雪绒花是一个徽章，被放置在某些维基百科编辑的个人资料页上。

sentences.en: The Edelweiss was a badge that was placed on the profile pages of some Wikipedia editors.
sentences.zh: 获奖者的名字也会被列入维基百科上介绍该奖项的页面中。

sentences.en: The names of winners were also included on a Wikipedia page that described the award.
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺和他的同事亚娜·加吕斯观察了获得雪绒花奖如何影响这些编辑的留存率，

sentences.en: Bruno and his colleague Jana Gallis observed how receiving an Edelweiss affected the retention rates for these editors
sentences.zh: 并将其与未获奖的编辑进行了对比。

sentences.en: compared to those who had not received one.
sentences.zh: 此前，只有35%的人继续为维基百科工作，并贡献了另一篇文章或协助处理了一篇文章。

sentences.en: Previously, 35% only continued working for Wikipedia and contributed another article or helped work with an article.
sentences.zh: 而这个数字从35%上升到了42%。

sentences.en: And this rose from 35% to 42%.
sentences.zh: 因此，很大一部分参与维基百科的人被引导继续这项工作。

sentences.en: So a much larger proportion of people engaged in Wikipedia were induced to go on with the work.
sentences.zh: 当然，有人可能会说，从35%到42%并不是天翻地覆的变化。

sentences.en: Now, of course, someone can say 35% to 42% is not a sea change.
sentences.zh: 但相对而言，这种干预的成本很低，很便宜。

sentences.en: But, of course, the intervention is relatively inexpensive and cheap.
sentences.zh: 你基本上只是给予某人一份认可、一个头衔。

sentences.en: You're basically giving someone a recognition, a title.
sentences.zh: 维基百科并没有给他们钱。

sentences.en: Wikipedia is not giving them money.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一件相对容易做到的事情。

sentences.en: It's actually relatively easy to do.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的观点。

sentences.en: That's a very important point.
sentences.zh: 这个雪绒花奖绝对、完全不需要任何成本。

sentences.en: This Edelweiss award is absolutely, doesn't cost anything.
sentences.zh: 你只需把它放到网页上即可。

sentences.en: You just put it on the web.
sentences.zh: 但人们真的很感激这一点。

sentences.en: But people really appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 因此，工作留存率的这种提升，尤其是新人的留存率，相当可观。

sentences.en: And so this increase in retentions for the work, especially of newcomers, is quite substantial.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，幅度这么大令人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And to me, it was surprising that it was so large.
sentences.zh: 大多数奖项都是为了被严肃对待而设立的。

sentences.en: Most awards are meant to be taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 但现在有一种日益增多的奖项类型，它们旨在具有讽刺意味。

sentences.en: But there's a growing genre of awards that are meant to be ironic.
sentences.zh: 比如搞笑诺贝尔奖，它表彰那些让人捧腹大笑的科学创新。

sentences.en: There's the Ig Nobel Prize, which recognizes innovations in science that make you laugh.
sentences.zh: 还有金酸莓奖，每年颁发给好莱坞最烂的电影。

sentences.en: And there's the Razzie, which is given to the worst Hollywood films each year.
sentences.zh: 2002年，哈莉·贝瑞凭借在电影《死囚之舞》中的表演赢得了奥斯卡奖。

sentences.en: In 2002, Halle Berry won an Oscar for her performance in the movie Monster's Ball.
sentences.zh: 三年后，她主演了《猫女》。

sentences.en: Three years later, she starred in Catwoman.
sentences.zh: 因为那个角色，她得到的不是奥斯卡奖，而是金酸莓奖。

sentences.en: For that role, she received not an Oscar, but a Razzie.
sentences.zh: 我有太多人需要感谢，因为没有很多人给予的大力帮助，你是赢不了金酸莓奖的。

sentences.en: I've got so many people to thank because you don't win a Razzie without a lot of help from a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，我要感谢华纳兄弟公司。

sentences.en: So, first of all, I want to thank Warner Brothers.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们让我参演了一部糟糕透顶的烂片。

sentences.en: Thank you for putting me in a piece of God awful movie.
sentences.zh: 那么，布鲁诺，像金酸莓奖或搞笑诺贝尔奖这样讽刺性的奖项究竟有什么作用？

sentences.en: So, Bruno, what do ironic awards like the Razzie or the Ig Nobel Prize, what do they do?
sentences.zh: 它们如何影响人类行为？

sentences.en: How do they affect human behavior?
sentences.zh: 当某样东西非常重要时，比如诺贝尔奖或学院奖、奥斯卡奖，做完全相反的事情总是很有吸引力。

sentences.en: When something is very important, such as a Nobel Prize or Academy Awards, Oscars, it's always attractive to do exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 这个金合金树莓奖正是普通奥斯卡奖的反面。

sentences.en: And this Golden Raspberry Award is exactly the opposite of the normal Oscar.
sentences.zh: 成为最差男演员或最差女演员同样能吸引关注。

sentences.en: To be the worst actor or the worst actress is also giving attention.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人能像我们刚才听到的这位女演员那样，以如此美妙的方式接受这个负面奖项，这对她大有好处。

sentences.en: And if one accepts this negative award in such a fantastic way as the actress we just heard, it's very good for her.
sentences.zh: 因为这样人们会说她是一个思想开放的人，这为她增添了积极的光彩。

sentences.en: Because then people say she's an open person and that throws a positive light on her.
sentences.zh: 当然，在这种情况下，感谢华纳兄弟实际上是一种含沙射影的方式，意思是华纳兄弟拍了一部可怕的电影。

sentences.en: Of course, in this case, thanking Warner Brothers is sort of a backhanded way of saying Warner Brothers made a terrible movie.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，是的。

sentences.en: Exactly, yes.
sentences.zh: 她以一种非常迷人的方式做到了这一点，这太棒了。

sentences.en: She did it in a very charming way and that's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 任何研究人类行为的人都知道，人们并不总是按常理出牌。

sentences.en: Anyone who studies human behavior knows that people don't always act predictably.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨奖项有时如何适得其反，以及我们如何才能更好地设计奖项。

sentences.en: When we come back, how awards can sometimes backfire and what we can do to design them better.
sentences.zh: 企业奖项很容易成为电视节目中喜剧嘲讽的目标。

sentences.en: Corporate awards can be an easy target for comedy on TV shows.
sentences.zh: 情景喜剧《办公室》里的常驻笑话之一就是邓迪奖。

sentences.en: One of the running jokes on the sitcom The Office was the Dundee Awards.
sentences.zh: 邓迪奖是颁发给故事发生地的造纸公司——邓德·米夫林员工的年度奖项。

sentences.en: The Dundees were an annual prize given to employees at Dunder Mifflin, the paper company where the show was set.
sentences.zh: 邓迪奖关乎我们每个人身上最好的一面。

sentences.en: The Dundees are about the best in every one of us.
sentences.zh: 该剧的粉丝都会记得，邓迪奖是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Fans of the show will remember that the Dundees were a train wreck.
sentences.zh: 办公室主管迈克尔·斯科特在其中让自己和所有其他人都感到极其尴尬。

sentences.en: One in which the head of the office, Michael Scott, humiliated himself along with everyone else.
sentences.zh: 你不需要成为邓德·米夫林的员工也知道奖项会产生适得其反的效果。

sentences.en: You don't have to be an employee of Dunder Mifflin to know that awards can backfire.
sentences.zh: 有时它们会以有趣的方式适得其反。

sentences.en: Sometimes they backfire in interesting ways.
sentences.zh: 例如，研究人员卡莉·鲁宾逊和亚娜·加吕斯最近追踪了加利福尼亚州一个学区的1.5万名初高中学生。

sentences.en: For example, the researchers Carly Robinson and Yana Gallas recently tracked 15,000 middle and high school students in a California school district.
sentences.zh: 该学区一直在向出勤率完美的学生颁发奖项。

sentences.en: The school system was giving out awards to students who had perfect attendance.
sentences.zh: 卡莉说，出乎所有人的意料，获得这些奖项的孩子去学校的次数反而减少了。

sentences.en: Carly says, to everyone's surprise, the kids who got these awards began attending school less often.
sentences.zh: 当学生们收到这些追溯性奖项时，这向他们传递了一个信号：他们的上学频率比同龄人更高。

sentences.en: When students receive these retrospective awards, it signals to them that they were attending school more than their classmates.
sentences.zh: 并且这个奖项可能还暗示了学校对他们的出勤率抱有很低的期望。

sentences.en: And this award also potentially signals that the school had low expectations for their attendance.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们实际上超出了学校对自己出勤率的预期。

sentences.en: So they were actually overshooting their school's expectations for their own attendance.
sentences.zh: 那么，布鲁诺，这个故事告诉我们关于获奖者并不总是能从奖项中获得颁奖者意图的什么信息？

sentences.en: So, Bruno, what does this story tell us about how recipients don't always take away from an award what givers intend?
sentences.zh: 人不应该因为属于自己日常活动正常部分的事情而获奖，因为那样奖项就会失去意义。

sentences.en: One should not get an award for something which is the normal part of one's activities, because then they lose their meaning.
sentences.zh: 奖项真正应该表明或暗示的是，一个人做了非凡的事情，而这种事情并非由外界规定或强加的。

sentences.en: An award should really indicate or signal that one does something extraordinary, which is not described or imposed from outside.
sentences.zh: 而这种事情并非由外界规定或强加的。

sentences.en: That really comes from a special engagement.
sentences.zh: 这确实源于一种特殊的承诺。

sentences.en: If one hands out an award for just everything, they lose their special character.
sentences.zh: 如果对什么都颁发奖项，它们就会失去原本的特殊意义。

sentences.en: There's the example of the Purple Heart, which is a very important American award.
sentences.zh: 紫心勋章就是一个例子，这是一项非常重要的美国奖项。

sentences.en: It was given three times in the American Revolutionary War.
sentences.zh: 它在美国独立战争期间颁发过三次。

sentences.en: Contrast that with World War II, where the number of Purple Hearts awarded by the United States was larger by orders of magnitude.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，在第二次世界大战中，美国颁发的紫心勋章数量增加了几个数量级。

sentences.en: And you see here the huge inflation.
sentences.zh: 你在这里可以看到巨大的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And that means, of course, that a Purple Heart does not have the importance it used to have in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着紫心勋章已经失去了它过去拥有的重要性。

sentences.en: So, in some ways, what you're saying is when awards are scarce, people actually look at them and they have value.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，你的意思是，当奖项稀缺时，人们才会真正关注它们，它们才具有价值。

sentences.en: But you can actually devalue an award by giving out too many of them.
sentences.zh: 但如果颁发太多，实际上反而会贬低奖项的价值。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，是的。

sentences.en: It's with everything.
sentences.zh: 做什么都是这样。

sentences.en: If one does it too much, it doesn't have any effect anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果做得太多，就不会再有任何效果了。

sentences.en: Let's look at another study.
sentences.zh: 让我们看另一项研究。

sentences.en: Kirk Doron and George Borjas found that winners of the Fields Medal, this was a prize for mathematicians under the age of 40, respond in some ways, like the students in California.
sentences.zh: 柯克·多伦和乔治·博贾斯发现，菲尔兹奖的得主——这是一项针对40岁以下数学家的奖项——在某些方面的反应，就像加州的那些学生一样。

sentences.en: Compared to mathematicians who nearly win but don't, the winners end up dabbling in new areas of mathematics where they end up being less successful.
sentences.zh: 与那些差一点获奖但最终没能获奖的数学家相比，获奖者最后往往会涉足他们不太成功的新的数学领域。

sentences.en: Here's Doron.
sentences.zh: 多伦是这么说的。

sentences.en: I think it's not what John Charles Fields expected.
sentences.zh: 我认为这并不是约翰·查尔斯·菲尔兹所期望的。

sentences.en: He expected that in giving people a prize to honor and extol their previous work, that would encourage them to do more of the same work.
sentences.zh: 他期望通过颁发奖项来表彰和赞誉他们先前的研究，从而鼓励他们做出更多类似的研究。

sentences.en: What we find is that, you know, the opposite takes place.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现，你懂的，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: What do you make of this, Bruno?
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺，你怎么看这件事？

sentences.en: No, in some ways, this paper was arguing that the mathematicians who nearly win, they're tipped to be winners of the Fields Medal.
sentences.zh: 不，在某种程度上，这篇论文认为，那些险些获奖的数学家其实被看好是菲尔兹奖的得主。

sentences.en: But since the medal is given only to people under the age of 40, there are people who pass the age of 40 without winning it.
sentences.zh: 但由于该奖项只颁发给40岁以下的人，有些人还没获奖就超过了40岁。

sentences.en: But ironically, it finds that those people end up being more productive, at least as measured by the number of papers they write.
sentences.zh: 但具有讽刺意味的是，研究发现这些人最终产量更高，至少从他们撰写的论文数量来衡量是这样的。

sentences.en: So in some ways, the award is actually not producing what the originator of the award intended.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，该奖项实际上并没有产生奖项创始人的初衷。

sentences.en: It didn't produce with the recipients of the Fields Medal, but with the others.
sentences.zh: 它没有在菲尔兹奖得主身上产生这种效果，反而在其他人身上产生了。

sentences.en: So in a way, the purpose was reached.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，目的达到了。

sentences.en: And I think the others who didn't get the prize want to get recognition in some other way and therefore work hard while the recipients are satisfied.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些没有获奖的人希望以其他方式获得认可，因此努力工作，而获奖者则已经心满意足了。

sentences.en: Because a mathematician cannot get more than the Fields Prize.
sentences.zh: 因为数学家不可能获得比菲尔兹奖更高的荣誉了。

sentences.en: That's a fascinating idea in some ways.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来看，这是一个极其迷人的想法。

sentences.en: I think what you might be hinting at is that potentially the benefits of some awards might be seen more in the people who don't win the award because it motivates them to try harder.
sentences.zh: 我想你可能在暗示，某些奖项的好处可能更多地体现在那些没有获奖的人身上，因为这能激励他们加倍努力。

sentences.en: Even if they'd never win an award, it still helps the whole field because they're doing all this extra work.
sentences.zh: 即使他们永远不会获奖，它对整个领域仍然有帮助，因为他们付出了所有这些额外的努力。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对的，对的。

sentences.en: But that's not always the case.
sentences.zh: 但情况并非总是如此。

sentences.en: It's very often, or in many instances, when an award is given to some person or to some persons,
sentences.zh: 很多时候，或者在许多情况下，当一个奖项颁发给某个人或某些人时，

sentences.en: and those not getting an award may be getting mad or they think they are not appreciated.
sentences.zh: 那些没有获奖的人可能会生气，或者认为自己没有受到赏识。

sentences.en: So there's also this negative side about it.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是它消极的一面。

sentences.en: I remember reading a column by Paul Krugman.
sentences.zh: 我记得读过保罗·克鲁格曼的一篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: He was writing in the New York Times a few months ago, and he was talking about how people are often dissatisfied.
sentences.zh: 几个月前他在《纽约时报》上撰文，谈到了人们为何常常感到不满。

sentences.en: Even in the field of economics, he said there are people who are working at various universities who are envious of their colleagues who are working at Harvard and Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他说，即使在经济学领域，也有一些人在各所大学工作，他们嫉妒那些在哈佛和芝加哥工作的同事。

sentences.en: And the people who are working at Harvard and Chicago are envious of the people who've won the Nobel Prize and they haven't won it.
sentences.zh: 而在哈佛和芝加哥工作的人又嫉妒那些获得诺贝尔奖而他们没有获奖的人。

sentences.en: So even when you're at the very top of your game, you can find sources of resentment when you see that other people around you are doing even better.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你处于行业巅峰，当你看到身边的其他人做得更好时，你也能找到怨恨的根源。

sentences.en: I heard the story that a Nobel Prize winner, when he gets the Nobel Prize or she gets the Nobel Prize, starts thinking about the,
sentences.zh: 我听说过这样一个故事，一位诺贝尔奖得主在获得诺贝尔奖时，开始思考……

sentences.en: I think there are five people who got two Nobel Prizes.
sentences.zh: 我想有五个人获得了两次诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: There's no end to it.
sentences.zh: 这真是没完没了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In 2016, former British Prime Minister David Cameron was criticized for seeking to give high state honors to a bunch of cronies.
sentences.zh: 2016年，英国前首相大卫·卡梅伦因试图向一帮亲信授予高级国家荣誉而受到批评。

sentences.en: Among the list of recipients was Mrs. David Cameron's stylist, Isabel Spearman.
sentences.zh: 获奖名单中包括大卫·卡梅伦夫人的造型师伊莎贝尔·斯皮尔曼。

sentences.en: Here's what Tom Watson of the Labour Party had to say about David Cameron's awards liSt.
sentences.zh: 工党的汤姆·沃森对大卫·卡梅伦的授奖名单发表了以下看法。

sentences.en: I think people will be shocked at the scale and size of this liSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们会对这份名单的规模和体量感到震惊。

sentences.en: You know, there's a reasonableness test that should be applied to these lists.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些名单应该接受一项合理性测试。

sentences.en: And I think most reasonable people would say it's unacceptable to give Mrs. Cameron's stylist an OBE and to hand out knighthoods to members of Parliament like confetti.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数理性的人都会认为，授予卡梅伦夫人的造型师帝国勋章（OBE），并像天女散花一样向国会议员颁发爵士头衔，是不可接受的。

sentences.en: So it surely must be the case, Bruno, that award givers sometimes misuse their position to confer honor and legitimacy on their friends.
sentences.zh: 所以布鲁诺，颁奖者有时会滥用职权，为他们的朋友赋予荣誉和合法性，这绝对是肯定的吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: If that is done, if that is done, if that is done, that is a grave mistake.
sentences.zh: 如果这样做的话，如果这样做的话，如果这样做的话，那将是一个严重的错误。

sentences.en: So it's a bad policy, for instance, for a king or a queen to give it to people who are very much on their side, because then the award or the order given loses importance.
sentences.zh: 因此，举例来说，国王或女王把奖项颁给那些坚定支持他们的人并不是一个好政策，因为这样一来，所颁发的奖项或勋章就会失去重要性。

sentences.en: It would be a bad policy.
sentences.zh: 这将是一个糟糕的政策。

sentences.en: So there's a tension here, isn't it, which is if you've just come into power, you know, and I think you give the example of Hitler actually doing this with the Iron Cross,
sentences.zh: 所以这里存在一种紧张关系，对吧？也就是当你刚上台时，我知道你举了希特勒实际这样做的例子，也就是铁十字勋章，

sentences.en: which was also a medal that was given out very, it was very scarce initially.
sentences.zh: 这也是一枚颁发得非常……最初非常稀少的勋章。

sentences.en: And then once Hitler came to power, he sort of distributed it like candy in some ways to large numbers of people, if I recall correctly.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，一旦希特勒上掌权，他有点像发糖一样把勋章分发给大量的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But there must be a temptation to do this because you've come in and you want to solidify and strengthen your position.
sentences.zh: 但这样做一定有一种诱惑，因为你刚刚上台，想要巩固和加强你的地位。

sentences.en: And the cheapest and easiest thing to do is to just simply spew these awards around.
sentences.zh: 而最廉价、最简单的事情就是简单地把这些奖项大肆挥霍出去。

sentences.en: Yes, that is the problem.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Before we discussed that, a positive side of awards is that they don't cost much money.
sentences.zh: 在此之前我们讨论过，奖项的一个积极方面是它们不需要花太多钱。

sentences.en: But the negative side is that you can distribute heaps of them and it doesn't cost you anything, but it destroys the award.
sentences.zh: 但消极的一面是，你可以分发成堆的奖项，虽然不花你什么钱，但它毁了这个奖项。

sentences.en: If you can undermine an award by giving it out to undeserving people, Bruno says you can also undermine awards by doing exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺表示，如果你把奖项颁给不配的人从而破坏奖项，你也可以通过做完全相反的事情来破坏奖项。

sentences.en: If you give awards only to people who are already acknowledged superstars, this shuts the door to outsiders who may have truly revolutionary ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果你只把奖项颁给那些已经是公认的超级巨星的人，这就向可能拥有真正革命性想法局外人关上了大门。

sentences.en: Bruno cites the example of an extraordinary researcher who didn't win the Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺举了一个没有获得诺贝尔奖的非凡研究人员的例子。

sentences.en: The reason?
sentences.zh: 原因是什么？

sentences.en: He was also known as a blunt provocateur.
sentences.zh: 他也因直言不讳的挑衅者而闻名。

sentences.en: Gordon Tullock was a very extraordinary economiSt.
sentences.zh: 戈登·塔洛克是一位非常杰出的经济学家。

sentences.en: He was a professor of economics, but who was a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位经济学教授，但背景是律师。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that was the first thing that he is a little bit of an outsider.
sentences.zh: 是的，首先他有一点局外人的色彩。

sentences.en: He wrote with James Buchanan an important book in public choice.
sentences.zh: 他与詹姆斯·布坎南合著了一本关于公共选择的重要著作。

sentences.en: And then James Buchanan won the Nobel Prize, though much of the contribution of the book is due to Gordon Tullock.
sentences.zh: 然后詹姆斯·布坎南赢得了诺贝尔奖，尽管该书的大部分贡献归功于戈登·塔洛克。

sentences.en: And it's even written in the introduction that he contributed the major idea of the book.
sentences.zh: 甚至在前言中也写道，他贡献了这本书的主要思想。

sentences.en: And the reason he didn't get the prize was, I was told that by members of the Nobel Prize committee,
sentences.zh: 至于他为什么没有获奖，诺贝尔奖委员会的成员曾告诉我，

sentences.en: that they didn't know how he would behave when he gets the prize.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道他在获奖时会表现出什么样子。

sentences.en: Because the Nobel Prize winners afterwards give a talk of gratitude.
sentences.zh: 因为诺贝尔奖得主事后要发表致谢演讲。

sentences.en: And there was one example already that is Friedrich von Hayek.
sentences.zh: 而且已经有一个这样的先例，那就是弗里德里希·冯·哈耶克。

sentences.en: He got the Nobel Prize and then said the Nobel Prize is not a very good idea for economists.
sentences.zh: 他获得了诺贝尔奖，然后却说诺贝尔奖对经济学家来说并不是个好主意。

sentences.en: And of course, Nobel Prize Foundation didn't want to have a similar talk again.
sentences.zh: 当然，诺贝尔奖基金会不想再听到类似的演讲了。

sentences.en: So it was unclear how Gordon Tullock would behave, while James Buchanan, he was a southerly gentleman,
sentences.zh: 所以当时不清楚戈登·塔洛克会作何表现，而詹姆斯·布坎南是一位温文尔雅的南方绅士，

sentences.en: and everybody knew that he would behave in the appropriate way.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道他会表现得体。

sentences.en: You know, as we've been talking, I'm realizing how complicated this field is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我们的交谈中，我意识到这个领域有多么复杂。

sentences.en: Because in some ways, you are trying to manipulate people by giving them an award.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，你是试图通过颁发奖项来操纵人们。

sentences.en: At some level, you are trying to shape human behavior.
sentences.zh: 在某种水平上，你是在试图塑造人类的行为。

sentences.en: You're trying to recognize people who have done great work.
sentences.zh: 你是在试图认可那些做出伟大工作的人。

sentences.en: You're trying to inspire other people, but you're also trying to do it in a way that doesn't feel controlling,
sentences.zh: 你是在试图激励其他人，但你同时也想以一种不让人觉得被控制的方式来做到这一点，

sentences.en: which doesn't feel like you're actually manipulating people.
sentences.zh: 一种不让人觉得你实际上在操纵人们的方式。

sentences.en: So a good award inspires people and communicates sort of the norms of the organization
sentences.zh: 因此，一个好的奖项能够激励人们并传达某种组织的规范，

sentences.en: without necessarily feeling heavy-handed, even though it actually may have been designed,
sentences.zh: 而又不会让人觉得过于专断，尽管它实际上可能是经过精心设计的，

sentences.en: you know, in a fairly heavy-handed manner.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，以一种相当强势的方式。

sentences.en: There's a real paradox and tension there.
sentences.zh: 这里面存在着真正的悖论和张力。

sentences.en: Yes, indeed, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，是的。

sentences.en: It's difficult to give good awards,
sentences.zh: 要颁发出好的奖项是很困难的，

sentences.en: because one might also run the danger that one gives it to people who do not earn it or deserve it.
sentences.zh: 因为人们也可能会面临这样的危险：把奖颁给那些没有挣得或不配得到它的人。

sentences.en: And that's very bad for an award if it's given to people who didn't deserve it.
sentences.zh: 如果把奖项颁给不配的人，这对奖项本身来说是非常糟糕的。

sentences.en: And that's, of course, very bad for the giver of the award,
sentences.zh: 当然，这对于颁奖者来说也非常糟糕，

sentences.en: because it's no longer going to the right people.
sentences.zh: 因为奖项不再授予真正合适的人了。

sentences.en: You know, you've talked at various points, Bruno, about how money is not a very good reward.
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺，你曾在不同场合谈到金钱并不是一种很好的奖励。

sentences.en: In one of the early episodes of Hidden Brain, we interviewed someone who worked at a company.
sentences.zh: 在《隐秘大脑》早期的节目中，我们采访了一位在某家公司工作的人。

sentences.en: This person had an interesting idea.
sentences.zh: 这个人有一个有趣的想法。

sentences.en: Rather than give out cash awards, the person essentially set up,
sentences.zh: 这位公司老板没有发放现金奖励，而是设立了一个小基金，

sentences.en: this was the owner of the company, set up a little fund
sentences.zh: 在这个基金里，任何员工都可以给其他任何员工颁发现金奖。

sentences.en: where any employee could give any other employee a cash award.
sentences.zh: 这样做的好处是，颁发奖项的员工

sentences.en: And the benefit of doing this is the employee who was giving out the award
sentences.zh: 不仅可以因为良好的行为、出色的工作或卓越的服务而颁奖，

sentences.en: not only could give out an award for good behavior or work well done or exceptional service,
sentences.zh: 还必须写下他们为什么认为获奖者当之无愧的理由。

sentences.en: but also had to write up why they thought the recipient deserved the award.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这巩固了颁奖者和接收者对为什么要颁发这个奖项的共识。

sentences.en: So in some ways, it solidified both the giver as well as the receiver's sense of why the award was being given.
sentences.zh: 你认为这是将金钱作为激励工具的有效方法吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that's an effective way to use money as a motivational tool?
sentences.zh: 这确实非常有趣。

sentences.en: That's very interesting indeed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常符合奖项的本质，

sentences.en: I think this goes very much in the direction of awards,
sentences.zh: 也就是明确表达某人为什么能获得这笔额外的金钱。

sentences.en: namely that one expresses exactly why somebody gets this additional amount of money.
sentences.zh: 人们确实必须在更广泛的社会背景下去思考。

sentences.en: One really has to think in a more social context.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种以这种方式发钱的想法很有趣，

sentences.en: And I think this idea of handing out money in this way is interesting
sentences.zh: 而且绝对朝着正确的方向发展。

sentences.en: and certainly goes in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 但我会认为，如果员工可以互相颁发奖项，情况也会是一样的。

sentences.en: But I would argue that the same would be the case
sentences.zh: 我想通过谈论某个人的故事来结束关于奖项的讨论，

sentences.en: if employees could give other employees awards.
sentences.zh: 这个人冷落了世界上最著名的奖项，

sentences.en: I want to end this discussion about awards by talking about someone
sentences.zh: 当时诺贝尔委员会将诺贝尔文学奖授予了鲍勃·迪伦。

sentences.en: who dissed the world's most famous award
sentences.zh: 他直接无视了他们。

sentences.en: when the Nobel Committee awarded Bob Dylan the Nobel Prize in Literature.
sentences.zh: 喜剧演员蒂姆·海德克创作了这首极具迪伦风格的歌曲。

sentences.en: He simply ignored them.
sentences.zh: 宝贝，我不需要你的奖，我不需要你的奖。

sentences.en: The comedian Tim Heidecker composed this very Dylan-esque song.
sentences.zh: 看着我的眼睛，宝贝，看看我是多么鄙视这个奖，看看我是多么鄙视这个奖。

sentences.en: Well, I don't need your prize, babe, I don't need your prize.
sentences.zh: 布鲁诺，当有人拒绝一个奖项时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Just look into my eyes, babe, see how I despise the prize, see how I despise the prize.
sentences.zh: 我认为比鲍勃·迪伦这样不做反应更糟糕的，

sentences.en: So Bruno, what happens when someone rejects an award?
sentences.zh: 就是最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: I think even worse is not to react as Bob Dylan did.
sentences.zh: 至少拒绝它也是一种反应。

sentences.en: That is the worst thing.
sentences.zh: 总会有所发生，而如果只是说，哦，我得不得诺贝尔奖根本无关紧要，

sentences.en: To at least reject it is a reaction.
sentences.zh: 那才是最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Something happens, while to just say, oh, whether I get the Nobel Prize or not is totally irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 所以，当像鲍勃·迪伦这样的人拒绝像诺贝尔奖这样的奖项时，

sentences.en: That is the worst thing.
sentences.zh: 我们是否可以合理地猜测，摇滚歌手以后不太可能获得诺贝尔文学奖了？

sentences.en: So when someone like Bob Dylan rejects a prize like the Nobel Prize,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这不太可能。

sentences.en: is it fair to guess that rock singers are unlikely to get the Nobel Prize in literature going forward?
sentences.zh: 当然，委员会首先会与潜在获奖者交谈，

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's very unlikely.
sentences.zh: 非正式地询问他们是否会接受该奖项。

sentences.en: And of course, the committee first talks to potential recipients
sentences.zh: 这现在已经成了惯例，重要的奖项不会直接颁发。

sentences.en: and informally asks them whether they would accept the prize.
sentences.zh: 人们会事先沟通他们是否愿意接受，

sentences.en: And that is now the common procedure, that important prizes are not just given.
sentences.zh: 而当他们拒绝时，他们曾被选为潜在获奖者的消息就不会被泄露出去。

sentences.en: and when they say no, it's not revealed that they were chosen as possible recipients.
